test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
By interchanging the given two signs and two numbers (not digits), which of the following equations will NOT be correct?

× and –, 27 and 35

I. 27 ÷ 7 – 6 × 5 + 35 = 53

II. 11 – 7 + 35 × 420 ÷ 27 = 93
solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4671232025562bc3ba9a781319d633acf8cd8e78dc8e96912cd7564a7df4717d.png] 

Given conclusion I : 27 ÷ 7 – 6 × 5 + 35 = 53

By interchanging the given two signs × and – and two numbers 27 and 35 in the given equation the equation formed is as follows : 35 ÷ 7 × 6 - 5 + 27 = 53

⇒ __**35 ÷ 7**__ × 6 - 5 + 27 = 53

⇒ __**5 × 6**__ - 5 + 27 = 53

⇒ __**30**__ - 5 __**+ 27**__ = 53

⇒ __**57 - 5**__ = 53

⇒ 52 ≠ 53

LHS ≠ RHS

Given conclusion II : 11 – 7 + 35 × 420 ÷ 27 = 93

By interchanging the given two signs × and – and two numbers 27 and 35 in the given equation the equation formed is as follows : 11 × 7 + 27 - 420 ÷ 35 = 93

⇒ 11 × 7 + 27 - __**420 ÷ 35**__ = 93

⇒ __**1**____**1 × 7**__ + 27 - 12 = 93

⇒ __**77**____** + 27**__ - 12 = 93

⇒ __**104**____** - 12**__ = 93

⇒ 92 ≠ 93

LHS ≠ RHS

∴ Here, both conclusions I and II are not correct.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Both I and II".**
